title: This Mith Chowky Video Proves Even Thieves Can't Move In Mumbai Traffic, Internet Says 'Still Better Than Versova' | Viral News - News18
text: Mumbai traffic is known to be slow almost everywhere in the city, but people often point to Mith Chowky in Malad as one of the toughest spots to cross. The area is known for long jams that barely move and a recent video by actor and content creator Viraj Ghelani captured this problem in a funny way. In the clip, he is stuck in traffic when someone snatches his phone. His friend gets worried, but Viraj stays calm and even asks for food instead of panicking. His friend reminds him that the phone was costly, but Viraj confidently says he will get it back. A moment later, he finds the thief standing in the same jam, unable to run anywhere. The content creator simply takes his phone and jokingly reminds the thief that nobody can run away at Mith Chowky. Content Creator Highlights Mith Chowky’s Traffic Issue With A Funny Twist The clip starts with Viraj Ghelani talking on the phone when a thief on a two wheeler suddenly grabs it and goes away. Viraj stays calm, but the friend sitting next to him gets anxious, worried that the costly phone was stolen in broad daylight. Even as his friend panics, Viraj promises that he’ll get the phone back and continues chatting about something else. After a moment, he tells his friend he’s going to retrieve it. He then walks for a short distance and easily reaches the thief, who is stuck in the same long traffic line. Viraj takes his phone back and reminds the thief that escaping at Mith Chowky is nearly impossible. Before leaving, he also advises him to wear a helmet as a traffic cop is usually present at the signal. Sharing the clip on Instagram, Viraj Geelani wrote, “Mith Chowky is the safest place." Reacting to the post, a user wrote, “Reality of Mumbai. Wittiness with Sarcasm." Another shared, “Mith chowki is safer than Dubai." “This is the damn brutal truth of that MITH CHOWKI SIGNAL," a comment read. An individual stated, “Longest signal in Mumbai." Another mentioned, “Some great person once said that people’s hair has turned grey while waiting at Mith Chowki." One more added, “Based on a true incident." New Flyover Opened To Ease The Congestion To reduce heavy traffic at Mith Chowki, Union Minister Piyush Goyal opened a T-shaped flyover in January this year, following several delays. The bridge is 800 metres long and its eastern route starts from Girdhar Park. It ends near St. Joseph’s School, allowing vehicles to move towards Malad station and the Western Express Highway (WEH). Before the full opening, one section towards Malad station was launched earlier by Goyal and local MLA Aslam Shaikh in October 2024, but only light vehicles were allowed to use it at that time.
